title: Boundary and simplex-collapse test for simplicial realization functors
statement: A model category means a complete and cocomplete category $\mathcal M$ with classes $C,F,W$ of cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences. The class $W$ is retract closed and satisfies two-out-of-three, and $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system consists of factorizations of every map into its two classes, each class being exactly the maps with the diagonal-lifting property against the other. Trivial means also in $W$; an object is cofibrant if its initial map is in $C$, and fibrant if its terminal map is in $F$. Universes may be enlarged. Use the simplicial sets, standard simplices, boundaries and weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $V:\mathrm{sSet}\to\mathcal M$ preserve all small colimits. If $V(\partial\Delta^n)\to V(\Delta^n)$ is a cofibration for every $n\geq0$, then $V$ sends every monomorphism to a cofibration. If, in addition, every collapse $V(\Delta^n)\to V(\Delta^0)$ induced by $[n]\to[0]$ is a weak equivalence, then $V$ sends every monomorphism that is a weak homotopy equivalence to a trivial cofibration and sends every weak homotopy equivalence to a weak equivalence. In particular it sends every horn inclusion to a trivial cofibration. If $V$ has a right adjoint, this is a Quillen adjunction.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2 (boundary cellular generation), Proposition 3.6.8 and its horn-filtration induction, printed pp. 78-79 and 99 No Stacks tag states this homotopical result.

proof.text: Let $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be a monomorphism. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to obtain its relative skeletal filtration, whose stage $n$ attaches a small coproduct of copies of $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, and whose colimit is $Y$. Since $V$ preserves all small colimits, it preserves these coproducts, attaching pushouts, and the sequential colimit. Each image boundary map is a cofibration by hypothesis. The model-category axiom identifies $C$ with the left lifting class of $F\cap W$. Pushout closure is [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure], and transfinite-composition closure is [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting]. Coproduct closure follows directly from the lifting definition: a square from $\coprod_j f_j$ to a map $p$ restricts to a square from each $f_j$ to $p$; choose its filler $h_j$ and assemble them into $h$ by the coproduct universal property. The two filler equations hold after every coproduct injection, hence hold for $h$; this also covers the empty coproduct. Thus each image attaching map and their sequential composite belong to the left lifting class of $F\cap W$, so $V(i)$ is a cofibration. This includes $n=0$, where the boundary is empty; in particular it applies to every face, horn, and subcomplex inclusion used below.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2 and proof of Lemma 2.1.10; explicit boundary-cell transfer

proof.text: Assume the additional simplex-collapse hypothesis. Write $c_n:\Delta^n\to\Delta^0$ for the collapse. For any standard-simplex map $a:\Delta^k\to\Delta^n$, one has $c_n a=c_k$. Both $V(c_n)$ and $V(c_k)$ are weak equivalences, so two-out-of-three makes $V(a)$ a weak equivalence. This applies to all face inclusions and includes $n=0$, where the collapse is the identity.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.8, first sentence of the forward implication

proof.text:
We prove by induction on $n\geq1$ that $V(L)\to V(\Delta^n)$ is a weak equivalence whenever $L$ is the union of a nonempty proper set $S$ of codimension-one faces of $\Delta^n$. Denote the face omitting vertex $j$ by $F_j$. Thus $L=\bigcup_{j\in S}F_j$, and choose an omitted index $r\notin S$. In dimension one $S$ consists of one face, so the assertion is step 2. In dimension $n>1$, order the faces of $S$, start with a single face $F_j\cong\Delta^{n-1}$, and adjoin the others one at a time. The single-face case again follows from step 2. Suppose the faces indexed by a nonempty $A\subset S$ have been adjoined and the next face is $F_j$, with $j\in S\setminus A$. Its intersection with the preceding union is
$$K=F_j\cap\bigcup_{a\in A}F_a=\bigcup_{a\in A}(F_j\cap F_a).$$
Inside the simplex $F_j$, each $F_j\cap F_a$ is the face omitting vertex $a$ after reindexing the remaining vertices. These are distinct codimension-one faces. They form a nonempty proper collection because $A$ is nonempty and the face indexed by $r$ is absent. Hence the dimension-$n-1$ inductive hypothesis applies to $K\hookrightarrow F_j$. The displayed intersection identity is degreewise the identity for subsets of the vertex set: a simplex in $F_j$ is in the old union exactly when it omits at least one of the indices in $A$. The union square with corners $K,F_j,L_{\mathrm{old}},L_{\mathrm{old}}\cup F_j$ is a pushout, since in each degree it glues two subsets along their intersection. Its simplicial operators respect these inclusions; the resulting degreewise gluing has the pushout universal property for simplicial maps.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.8, induction setup and elementary face-intersection and gluing identities; the non-elementary lifting input is applied in step 4

proof.text: In the attaching square of step 3, $V(K)\to V(F_j)$ is a weak equivalence by the dimension-$n-1$ inductive hypothesis and a cofibration by step 1. It is therefore in $C\cap W$, the left lifting class of $F$. Preservation of the square by $V$ and pushout closure from [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] make $V(L_{\mathrm{old}})\to V(L_{\mathrm{old}}\cup F_j)$ a trivial cofibration. The inductive knowledge that $V(L_{\mathrm{old}})\to V(\Delta^n)$ is a weak equivalence and two-out-of-three now give the assertion for the enlarged union. This completes the finite attachment induction and then the dimension induction. Taking $S=\{0,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{r\}$ gives exactly the horn $\Lambda_r^n$ defined in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Thus $V(\Lambda_r^n)\to V(\Delta^n)$ is a weak equivalence; it is a cofibration by step 1, hence a trivial cofibration. No closure of arbitrary weak equivalences under pushouts is used: the attaching maps have first been proved trivial cofibrations.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.8, completion of the horn induction; Corollary 1.1.11

proof.text: Let $i$ be a simplicial monomorphism that is a weak homotopy equivalence. In [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] it is a trivial cofibration, and the same node states that every such map is an arrow retract of a transfinite composite of pushouts of coproducts of horn inclusions. The functor $V$ preserves the coproducts, pushouts and continuous ordinal colimits in this construction and preserves its retraction equations. Step 4 sends the generating horns into $C\cap W={}^{\square}F$. Closure of this left lifting class under pushouts and arrow retracts is [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]; transfinite-composition closure is [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting]. For coproduct closure, restrict any lifting square against $p\in F$ to its summands, choose the fillers $h_j$, and use the coproduct universal property to obtain $h$; both triangle equations hold on each summand and therefore on the coproduct. Applying these closures to the image construction proves that $V(i)$ is a trivial cofibration.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.8, passage from generating horns to trivial cofibrations; Theorem 3.6.5 and Lemma 2.1.10

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ now be any weak homotopy equivalence. Every simplicial set is cofibrant in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], since its initial map is degreewise injective. The cofibrant clause of [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] gives $X\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y$ and $s:Y\to Z$, where $i,s$ are cofibrations, $p$ is a trivial fibration, $pi=f$ and $ps=1_Y$. Two-out-of-three in simplicial sets makes $i$ and $s$ weak equivalences, hence trivial cofibrations. Step 5 makes $V(i)$ and $V(s)$ weak equivalences. Since $V(p)V(s)=1$, two-out-of-three in $\mathcal M$ makes $V(p)$ a weak equivalence; finally $V(f)=V(p)V(i)$ is a weak equivalence. This proves the arbitrary-map clause without assuming that $V$ preserves fibrations.

source.place: Lemma 1.1.12, Ken Brown argument using the existing split factorization

proof.text: If $V\dashv U$, steps 1 and 5 say exactly that the left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, which is the definition of a Quillen adjunction. Explicitly, a square with left map $i$ in simplicial sets and right map $U(p)$ corresponds under the adjunction to a square with left map $V(i)$ and right map $p$. The adjunction bijections send a diagonal $h$ to its adjoint and preserve the two required triangle equations by naturality. For a fibration $p$ use trivial-cofibration $i$, and for a trivial fibration $p$ use cofibration $i$; the two weak factorization systems then give the corresponding right lifting properties for $U(p)$.

source.place: Definition 1.3.1 and Lemma 1.3.4; the lifting adjunction written explicitly

lean.statement: theorem simplicial_boundary_collapse_test {M : Type v} [Category.{w} M] [ModelCategory M] [HasLimitsOfSize.{max u w, max u w} M] [HasColimitsOfSize.{max u w, max u w} M] [HasFunctorialFactorization (cofibrations M) (trivialFibrations M)] [HasFunctorialFactorization (trivialCofibrations M) (fibrations M)] (V : SSet.{u} ⥤ M) [PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u} V] (hboundary : ∀ n : ℕ, Cofibration (V.map (SSet.boundary.{u} n).ι)) : (∀ {X Y : SSet.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y), Mono f → Cofibration (V.map f)) ∧ ((∀ n : ℕ, WeakEquivalence (V.map (SSet.stdSimplex.{u}.map (SimplexCategory.const ⦋n⦌ ⦋0⦌ 0)))) → (∀ {X Y : SSet.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y), Mono f → SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence f → Cofibration (V.map f) ∧ WeakEquivalence (V.map f)) ∧ (∀ {X Y : SSet.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y), SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence f → WeakEquivalence (V.map f)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)), Cofibration (V.map (SSet.horn.{u} (n + 1) i).ι) ∧ WeakEquivalence (V.map (SSet.horn.{u} (n + 1) i).ι)) ∧ ∀ (U : M ⥤ SSet.{u}) (_adj : V ⊣ U), (∀ {A B : M} (p : A ⟶ B), Fibration p → Fibration (U.map p)) ∧ (∀ {A B : M} (p : A ⟶ B), trivialFibrations M p → SSet.modelCategoryQuillen.I.rlp (U.map p)))
